AD.description: Andorra lies high in the Pyrenees between France and Spain. Its mountain valleys are dotted with Romanesque churches, stone villages, and ski slopes.

photo.credit:
Andorra_la_Vella_-_view2.jpg: Tiia Monto
derivative work: Jjtkk
photo.alt: View from a northern side of the Andorra la Vella.

AE.description: The United Arab Emirates sits on the Arabian Peninsula, where desert dunes and historic trading ports contrast with Dubai’s skyscrapers and Abu Dhabi’s grand mosques.

photo.alt: Dubai Skyline

AF.description: Afghanistan is a mountainous country in Central and South Asia. Its heritage includes Bamiyan’s Buddhist remains, Silk Road trading cities, and the turquoise lakes of Band-e Amir.

photo.alt:
Wikivoyage banner: Band-e Amir Lake, meaning “Commander’s Dam”–a reference to the Commander of the Faithful, Imam Ali, the first imam of the Shia Muslims and the fourth Caliph of the Sunni Muslims)) refers to five lakes high in the Hindu Kush Mountains of Central Afghanistan at approximately 3000 meters elevation, west of the famous Buddhas of Bamiyan. They were created by the carbon dioxide rich water oozing out of the faults and fractures to deposit calcium carbonate precipitate in the form of travertine walls that today store the water of these lakes.
Photo by Nasim Fekrat of Afghanistan.

AG.description: Antigua and Barbuda is a Caribbean island country known for sheltered bays, Antigua’s historic English Harbour, and Barbuda’s pink sand beaches and frigatebird colony.

photo.credit:
Antigua_beach_view.jpg: Z_dead from London, UK
derivative work: Jjtkk
photo.alt: Country landscape banner from Wikivoyage

AI.description: Anguilla is a low-lying island in the eastern Caribbean. It is known for long white sand beaches, turquoise bays, and a musical tradition rooted in island life.

photo.alt: Blowing Point Ferry Terminal, Anguilla; Anguilla banner

AL.description: Albania sits on the Adriatic and Ionian seas in southeastern Europe, with Ottoman-era towns such as Berat, rugged mountain valleys, and the archaeological remains of Butrint.

photo.alt: Albania, Berat, Panorama

AM.description: Armenia is a mountainous country in the South Caucasus. Its landscape is marked by medieval stone monasteries, carved khachkar crosses, and the high-altitude waters of Lake Sevan.

photo.credit:
Noravank_panorama.jpg: Alexander Naumov
derivative work: Inkey
photo.alt: Panorama of the Armenian monastery Noravank in Armenia's mountainous Vayots Dzor region.

AO.description: Angola stretches along southern Africa’s Atlantic coast. It is known for the dramatic Kalandula Falls, the rocky formations of Pedras Negras, and the coastal landscapes near Namibe.

photo.credit:
Kalandula_waterfalls_of_the_Lucala-River_in_Malange,_Angola.JPG: Paulo César Santos
derivative work: Jjtkk
photo.alt: Kalandula waterfalls of Lucala river, Malange, Angola

AQ.description: Antarctica surrounds the South Pole, with vast ice sheets, mountain ranges, and coastal penguin colonies. Research stations support scientific work across this remote continent.

photo.alt: Adelie penguin on an iceberg near the Antarctic Peninsula; Antarctica banner

AR.description: Argentina extends from subtropical northern forests to Patagonia’s glaciers. It is known for Buenos Aires tango, Mendoza’s vineyards, and the waterfalls of Iguazú.

photo.alt: Fitz Roy massif, El Chaltén, Patagonia, Argentina

AS.description: American Samoa is a group of islands in the South Pacific. Volcanic ridges, tropical rainforest, and coral reefs sit alongside Samoan traditions of extended family and village life.

photo.alt: Ofu-Olosega, American Samoa. Ofu (left) and Olosega (right) are separated by a narrow strait just left of the center; American Samoa banner

AT.description: Austria is a Central European country shaped by the Alps and the Danube. It is known for Vienna’s classical music heritage, Salzburg’s Baroque streets, and Alpine lakes.

photo.alt: Hallstatt, Austria; Austria ToC banner

AU.description: Australia spans tropical reefs, red desert interiors, and temperate coastlines. Its distinctive features include the Great Barrier Reef, Uluru, and the enduring cultures of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.

photo.alt: Panoramic view of Kata-Tjuta in the early morning. This shows the extent of the southern vista of the rock formation. Stitched panorama image taken from the sunrise viewing platform.

AW.description: Aruba lies in the southern Caribbean near Venezuela. Its dry landscape features divi-divi trees and cacti, contrasting with white sand beaches and Oranjestad’s colorful buildings.

photo.alt: Panoramic View of Palm Beach Aruba from Gilians; Aruba banner

AX.description: The Åland Islands form a Swedish-speaking archipelago between Sweden and Finland. Red granite shores, sailing traditions, and Mariehamn’s maritime heritage give the islands their character.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner for Åland. Cropped from this PD-licensed picture: http://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Archipelago062009.jpg

AZ.description: Azerbaijan lies between the Caucasus Mountains and the Caspian Sea. It is known for Baku’s walled old city, Gobustan’s rock carvings, and landscapes dotted with mud volcanoes.

photo.credit:
Azerbajiani_landscape_-_Another_version.jpg: *Original: Matthew Hadley (nickname diff_sky)
derivative work: Ximonic (talk), Simo Räsänen
derivative work: Inkey
photo.alt: Landscape of Khinalug valley in Azerbaijan.

BA.description: Bosnia and Herzegovina is a mountainous Balkan country. Sarajevo’s Ottoman-era bazaar, Mostar’s stone bridge, and clear rivers reflect its layered cultural and architectural heritage.

photo.credit:
Goran Anđelić

Derivative work by Globe-trotter
photo.alt: Trebinje river panorama, Herzegovina

BB.description: Barbados is an eastern Caribbean island known for Bridgetown’s historic buildings, coral limestone caves, and a long rum-making tradition. Its Atlantic coast is shaped by strong surf.

photo.credit: Berit Watkin, derivative work (crop) by Globe-trotter
photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner of Barbados.

BD.description: Bangladesh occupies much of the Ganges–Brahmaputra delta in South Asia. It is known for the Sundarbans mangrove forest, intricate river networks, and Dhaka’s colorful rickshaw art.

photo.alt: Ratargul

BE.description: Belgium is a small Western European country known for medieval trading cities, Art Nouveau architecture, and distinctive brewing traditions. Bruges’ canals and Brussels’ Grand-Place are notable landmarks.

photo.alt: Cropped version of http://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Bruges.jpg

BF.description: Burkina Faso is a landlocked West African country with strong traditions of filmmaking, music, and craftsmanship. Bobo-Dioulasso’s earthen mosque and the painted architecture of Tiébélé are distinctive landmarks.

photo.alt: The Grand Mosque of Bobo-Dioulasso, Bukina Faso.

BG.description: Bulgaria stretches from the Balkan Mountains to the Black Sea. It is known for Rila Monastery, Thracian archaeological sites, and the rose-growing valleys around Kazanlak.

photo.alt: Beklemeto-pass panorama, Bulgaria

BH.description: Bahrain is an island country in the Persian Gulf. Its history centers on the ancient Dilmun civilization, maritime trade, and a pearling heritage preserved in Muharraq.

photo.credit:
Bahrain_Fort_8.jpg: Peter from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
derivative work: Jjtkk
photo.alt: The Manama city skyline is just to the left of this view.

BI.description: Burundi lies in East Africa’s Great Lakes region, with hills descending toward Lake Tanganyika. It is known for the ceremonial performances of its royal drumming tradition.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner for Burundi. Cropped from this PD-licensed picture: File:Burundi_Beach.JPG

BJ.description: Benin is a West African country known for the royal history of Abomey, the lake village of Ganvié, and Vodun traditions that remain part of its cultural life.

photo.credit:
Voodoo_Temple_(Ouidah,_Benin).jpg: Shubert Ciencia
derivative work: JamesA
photo.alt: A voodoo temple now stands guard in the hallowed grounds of the Door of No Return along Benin's Atlantic coast. The Door of No Return has been declared as a UNESCO world heritage site. Taken in 2007 with a Nikon D40 while attending the INAFI International Conference on Microfinance, Migration and Development.

BL.description: Saint Barthélemy is a small island in the northeastern Caribbean. It is known for Gustavia’s harbor, sheltered beaches, and a landscape of dry hills and red-roofed houses.

photo.alt: Saint Barth - Vue panoramique - Octobre 2009; Saint Barts banner

BM.description: Bermuda is an island group in the North Atlantic, known for pink sand beaches, limestone caves, and white-roofed houses designed to collect rainwater.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner for Bermuda. Cropped from this PD-licensed picture:http://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:View_from_top_of_Gibbs_Lighthouse_Bermuda.jpg

BN.description: Brunei lies on the island of Borneo in Southeast Asia. It is known for ornate mosques, the stilt houses of Kampong Ayer, and the rainforest of Ulu Temburong.

photo.alt: The panorama of 2013 Brunei Regatta.

BO.description: Bolivia spans Andean highlands and Amazonian lowlands. It is known for the Salar de Uyuni salt flat, Lake Titicaca, and the indigenous cultural traditions of the Altiplano.

photo.credit: Martin St-Amant (S23678); derivative work (noise reduction to sky) by Julia W
photo.alt: Incahuasi Island, in the middle of the Salar de Uyuni

BQ.description: Bonaire, Saint Eustatius, and Saba are three Caribbean islands with contrasting landscapes: Bonaire’s coral reefs and salt pans, Saint Eustatius’s volcanic crater, and Saba’s steep green slopes.

photo.credit: David Burley (User: (WT-shared) Khemicals at  wts wikivoyage)
photo.alt: Salt Piles, Island of Bonaire; Bonaire banner

BR.description: Brazil covers much of South America, from the Amazon rainforest to Atlantic beaches. It is known for samba, Rio de Janeiro’s mountain-framed coastline, and diverse regional cuisines.

photo.credit:
GRES Acadêmicos do Salgueiro Carnaval 2010 080 (5192038529).jpg Team at Carnaval.com Studios from The Inner Mission San Francisco
derivative work: ויקיג'אנקי

BS.description: The Bahamas is an Atlantic archipelago southeast of Florida. Its islands are known for shallow turquoise banks, blue holes, coral reefs, and the colorful costumes of Junkanoo celebrations.

photo.alt: Ariel Shot of Blue Lagoon Island

BT.description: Bhutan is a Himalayan country known for cliffside monasteries, fortress-like dzongs, and masked dances at religious festivals. Tiger’s Nest monastery overlooks the forested Paro Valley.

photo.credit:
The Tiger's Nest ( Paro Taktsang ).jpg: VIkramjit Kakati
derivative work: ויקיג'אנקי
photo.alt: Paro Taktsang (spa phro stag tshang / spa gro stag tshang), is the popular name of Taktsang Palphug Monastery (also known as The Tiger's Nest),[1] a prominent Himalayan Buddhist sacred site and temple complex, located in the cliffside of the upper Paro valley, Bhutan. A temple complex was first built in 1692, around the Taktsang Senge Samdup (stag tshang seng ge bsam grub) cave where Guru Padmasambhava is said to have meditated for three years, three months, three weeks, three days and three hours in the 8th century. Padmasambhava is credited with introducing Buddhism to Bhutan and is the tute

BV.description: Bouvet Island is a remote volcanic island in the South Atlantic. Ice-covered slopes and rocky shores provide breeding grounds for seals, penguins, and other seabirds.

photo.alt: For use at voy:Bouvet Island.

BW.description: Botswana is a landlocked southern African country known for the seasonal waterways of the Okavango Delta, the Kalahari Desert, and the elephants of the Chobe region.

photo.credit:
Tsodilo_Hills_rock_paintings5.jpg: Joachim Huber
derivative work: Jjtkk
photo.alt: Rock paintings in Tsodilo Hills, Botswana

BY.description: Belarus lies in Eastern Europe, with extensive forests, lakes, and wetlands. It is known for the castles of Mir and Nesvizh and the ancient woodland of Belovezhskaya Pushcha.

photo.alt: Panoramic view of Strusta Lake, Braslau Lakes, Belarus

BZ.description: Belize sits on Central America’s Caribbean coast. It is known for its barrier reef and Great Blue Hole, Maya archaeological sites, and Garifuna music and cultural traditions.

photo.credit:
BZECAYE09.jpg: Josh Steinitz from San Francisco, CA, USA
derivative work: Danapit
photo.alt: Beach on caye in Belize.

CA.description: Canada stretches between the Atlantic, Pacific, and Arctic oceans. Its landscapes include the Rocky Mountains and boreal forests, while Québec’s historic cities preserve a distinctive French-speaking heritage.

photo.alt: File:Herbert Lake beim Icefields Parkway.jpg resized and cropped for use as a Wikivoyage banner

CC.description: The Cocos (Keeling) Islands are coral atolls in the Indian Ocean. Coconut palms, shallow lagoons, and the Cocos Malay community distinguish this remote island group.

photo.alt: Country landscape banner from Wikivoyage

CD.description: The Democratic Republic of the Congo spans much of the Congo Basin in Central Africa. It is known for rainforest wildlife, the Congo River, and influential Congolese rumba music.

photo.alt: A panorama of the Lomami River at Katopa Camp, Democratic Republic of the Congo.

CF.description: The Central African Republic lies between tropical forests and savannas. The Dzanga-Sangha region is known for forest elephants gathering in clearings and the cultural traditions of Ba’Aka communities.

photo.credit: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Headquarters
photo.alt: Credit: Daphne Carlson Bremer/USFWS

CG.description: The Republic of the Congo lies along Central Africa’s Atlantic coast. It is known for the forests of Odzala-Kokoua, western lowland gorillas, and Brazzaville’s riverside setting.

photo.credit:
File:Sunrise on the Congo River - 2.JPG: Bsm15
derivative work: Lkcl it
photo.alt: Congo River and the Congo Rainforest — in the Republic of the Congo.

CH.description: Switzerland is an Alpine country in Central Europe, known for mountain railways, glacial lakes, and cheese-making traditions. Its German-, French-, Italian-, and Romansh-speaking regions have distinct cultural identities.

photo.credit:
Waldemmental_Juli2007.jpg: Simon Koopmann
derivative work: Jjtkk
photo.alt: View from Salwiden, above Sörenberg, to the mountains of the valley of Waldemme (Mariental) (left side: Schwändeliflue and Fürstein, middle: Hagleren and Nünalpstock, right side: Glaubenbielenpass), Entlebuch region, Switzerland

CI.description: Côte d’Ivoire lies on West Africa’s Gulf of Guinea. It is known for Grand-Bassam’s historic streets, the forests of Taï National Park, and its cocoa-growing landscapes.

photo.alt: Beach in San Pédro.

CK.description: The Cook Islands are scattered across the South Pacific. Rarotonga’s volcanic interior and Aitutaki’s lagoon are complemented by Polynesian dance, drumming, and canoe traditions.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner: Beach in Cook Islands

CL.description: Chile runs along South America’s Pacific coast between the Andes and the ocean. It is known for the Atacama Desert, Patagonian fjords, and Rapa Nui’s moai statues.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner: view from (almost) the summit of the Lascar volcano, the most active volcano of the northern Chilean Andes. It has several eruptions per year, and smoke from the crater can be seen. This was taken at an altitude of 5500m.

CM.description: Cameroon spans Atlantic coast, rainforest, grasslands, and northern savannas. Its distinctive landscapes include volcanic Mount Cameroon, while the western highlands preserve elaborate royal and mask-making traditions.

photo.alt: Kribi beach

CN.description: China stretches from Himalayan peaks to Pacific coastlines. It is known for the Great Wall, the terracotta army at Xi’an, and culinary traditions that vary widely by region.

photo.alt: Cropped and touched-up version of http://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Nine_Dragon_Wall_in_Beihai_Park.JPG

CO.description: Colombia connects the Andes, Amazon, and Caribbean coast. It is known for mountain coffee farms, Cartagena’s walled streets, and musical traditions such as cumbia and vallenato.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner: El Desierto de Tatacoa, Colombia

CR.description: Costa Rica lies between the Caribbean Sea and Pacific Ocean. It is known for cloud forests, volcanic landscapes, and protected habitats home to sloths, toucans, and sea turtles.

photo.alt: Arenal volcano, Costa Rica

CU.description: Cuba is a Caribbean island country known for Havana’s historic architecture, son music, and tobacco-growing traditions. The limestone hills of Viñales rise above its western valleys.

photo.alt: A street in Trinidad, Cuba. Trinidad has been one of UNESCOs World Heritage sites since 1988.

CV.description: Cabo Verde is a volcanic Atlantic archipelago off West Africa. It is known for morna music, Fogo’s volcanic landscapes, and the mountain valleys of Santo Antão.

photo.credit:
Road_to_caldera_in_Fogo_&_Pico_de_Fogo,_2010_12.jpg: Ximonic, Simo Räsänen
derivative work: Jjtkk
photo.alt: A road leading to Fogo National Park (Parque Natural do Fogo) in 2010 December. Pico do Fogo (2,829 m) on the right is a stratovolcano.  This   file was uploaded  with Commonist.

CW.description: Curaçao lies in the southern Caribbean. It is known for Willemstad’s brightly painted waterfront, the island’s sheltered coves, and Papiamentu language and cultural traditions.

photo.alt: Tourist section of the Willemstad harbor in Curaçao; Curaçao banner

CX.description: Christmas Island lies in the Indian Ocean south of Java. It is known for tropical rainforest, rugged limestone cliffs, and the seasonal migration of red crabs toward the sea.

photo.alt: Christmas Island banner

CY.description: Cyprus is an eastern Mediterranean island known for ancient mosaics at Paphos, the painted churches of the Troodos Mountains, and a long tradition of halloumi cheese-making.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner for Cyprus. Cropped from this PD-licensed picture: http://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Vouni.jpg

CZ.description: Czechia is a Central European country known for Prague’s medieval streets, Bohemian castles, and a long brewing tradition. Moravia adds vineyard landscapes and distinctive regional folk culture.

photo.credit:
Myslivny_bozi_dar_lake.jpg: Rafael Brix
derivative work: Danapit
photo.alt: Water reservoir near Myslivny in the Ore Mountains, Czech Republic

DE.description: Germany lies in Central Europe, with landscapes ranging from the North Sea to the Alps. It is known for timber-framed towns, influential composers, and the Bauhaus design movement.

photo.alt: Cropped from File:Ötlingen - Panoramaansicht klein

DJ.description: Djibouti sits where the Red Sea meets the Gulf of Aden. It is known for the salt shores of Lake Assal and the limestone chimneys around Lake Abbe.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner for Djibouti. Cropped from this PD-licensed picture:http://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Lake_Assal_1-Djibouti.jpg

DK.description: Denmark links the Jutland peninsula with an archipelago of islands. It is known for Copenhagen’s harbor, Viking history, and a design tradition emphasizing simple, functional forms.

photo.alt: Vitsö

DM.description: Dominica is a mountainous Caribbean island known for rainforest, waterfalls, and the geothermal Boiling Lake. It is also home to the Kalinago Territory and its indigenous cultural heritage.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner: Dominica, Panorama

DO.description: The Dominican Republic occupies the eastern part of Hispaniola. It is known for merengue and bachata, Santo Domingo’s historic colonial district, and landscapes of beaches and mountain ranges.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner: Panoramic view of a beach on the Saona island, Dominican Republic.

DZ.description: Algeria stretches from the Mediterranean coast deep into the Sahara. It is known for the Roman ruins of Timgad, Algiers’ Casbah, and the rock art of Tassili n’Ajjer.

photo.credit:
Abderrahmane boudjenane (original)

This derivative work (cropped): SHB2000
photo.alt: Tahagart sud algériens

EC.description: Ecuador straddles the equator in South America, combining Andean highlands, Amazon rainforest, and Pacific coastline. Its Galápagos Islands are known for wildlife found nowhere else.

photo.alt: Indigenous people peeling maize while overlooking Quito from El Panecillo, Ecuador.

EE.description: Estonia lies on the Baltic Sea in Northern Europe. It is known for Tallinn’s medieval old town, peat bog landscapes, and a choral tradition celebrated through large song festivals.

photo.credit:
Karksi_panoraam.jpg: Andrus Uuetalu

EG.description: Egypt centers on the Nile Valley in northeastern Africa. It is known for the pyramids of Giza, ancient temples at Luxor, and the coral reefs of the Red Sea.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner for Egypt. Cropped from this PD-licensed picture:https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Camels_and_the_Pyramids_co-existing_for_centuries..JPG

EH.description: Western Sahara lies on Africa’s Atlantic coast, with extensive desert plains and dunes. The Dakhla peninsula shelters a large lagoon, while Sahrawi heritage includes poetry and tea ceremonies.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner for Western Sahara. Cropped from this PD-licensed picture:http://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Hospital_de_navarra_tifariti_rasd.jpg

ES.description: Spain occupies much of the Iberian Peninsula. It is known for Andalusian flamenco, Barcelona’s modernist architecture, and regional food traditions ranging from Basque pintxos to Valencian paella.

photo.credit:
Iglesia_de_Nuestra_Señora_de_La_Blanca,_Cardejón,_España,_2012-09-01,_DD_02.JPG: Poco a poco
derivative work: Jjtkk
photo.alt: Field of sunflowers (Helianthus annuus) with the church of Nuestra Señora de La Blanca in the background, Cardejón, Spain

ET.description: Ethiopia lies in the Horn of Africa, with dramatic highland plateaus and Rift Valley landscapes. It is known for Lalibela’s rock-hewn churches, ancient Aksum, and coffee ceremonies.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner of Ethiopia: landscape at Wunenia near Gondar

FI.description: Finland is a Northern European country of forests, lakes, and Baltic islands. Sauna culture, the northern lights of Lapland, and modern Finnish design are distinctive parts of its identity.

photo.alt: Sun setting over Lake Päijänne at Sysmä, Finland. On the right is Päijätsalo island which is part of the Päijätsalo natural park.

FJ.description: Fiji is a South Pacific archipelago known for coral reefs, volcanic highlands, and village traditions. Kava ceremonies and the cultural heritage of iTaukei and Indo-Fijian communities shape island life.

photo.alt: Shangri-La Fijian Resort, Fiji

FK.description: The Falkland Islands are a South Atlantic archipelago off southern South America. Windswept grasslands, penguin colonies, and offshore islands supporting albatrosses define their landscape.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner for Falkland Islands. Cropped from this PD-licensed picture:http://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Stanley-Airport.JPG

FM.description: The Federated States of Micronesia spans island groups in the western Pacific. It is known for Nan Madol’s stone ruins, Yap’s stone money, and longstanding ocean navigation traditions.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner for Federated States of Micronesia. Cropped from this PD-licensed picture:File:Falalop_Island-_Ulithi_Atoll.JPG

FO.description: The Faroe Islands lie in the North Atlantic between Iceland and Norway. Steep sea cliffs, grass-roofed houses, and villages beside narrow fjords give the archipelago its distinctive appearance.

photo.credit:
Gjogv_kløft_2.jpg: Lillestrøm SK
derivative work: Jjtkk
photo.alt: Bilde fra Gjógv på Færøyene. Bilde over juvet som har gitt navn til stedet.

FR.description: France stretches from Atlantic and Mediterranean coastlines to the Alps. It is known for Parisian art collections, Gothic cathedrals, and regional food and wine traditions.

photo.alt: The little village of Sainte-Enimie (Lozère, France) at the entrance of the Gorges du Tarn, seen from a picnic area on D986 road.

GA.description: Gabon lies on Central Africa’s Atlantic coast, with extensive equatorial rainforest. Loango’s coastal habitats and Lopé’s forest–savanna landscapes support elephants, primates, and other wildlife.

photo.alt: Stitched Panorama of Lopé National Park

GB.description: The United Kingdom includes England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland. It is known for London’s museums, medieval castles, the Scottish Highlands, and distinct literary and musical traditions.

photo.alt: Country landscape banner from Wikivoyage

GD.description: Grenada is a Caribbean island country known for nutmeg production, St. George’s colorful harbor, and volcanic scenery. The smaller islands of Carriacou and Petite Martinique preserve boatbuilding traditions.

photo.alt: Grenada, Port scenerie, Panorama

GE.description: Georgia lies in the South Caucasus, where mountain villages and medieval monasteries overlook deep valleys. It is known for qvevri wine-making and distinctive polyphonic singing.

photo.credit:
Kazbeg_Panorama.jpg: Philipp Weigell
derivative work: Inkey
photo.alt: 360-degree panoramic view of the Gergeti Trinity Church, the Mount Kazbek, and Mount Shani in Georgia

GF.description: French Guiana lies on South America’s Atlantic coast. Amazonian forests surround coastal settlements, while the Guiana Space Centre near Kourou connects the region with space exploration.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner for French Guiana. Cropped from this PD-licensed picture:http://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Bagne_Cayenne_03.jpg

GG.description: Guernsey lies in the Channel Islands near the French coast. It is known for St Peter Port’s harbor, coastal fortifications, and Victor Hugo’s former home at Hauteville House.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner for Guernsey. Cropped from this PD-licensed picture: http://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Guernsey_July_2010_Vale_Castle_10.jpg

GH.description: Ghana lies on West Africa’s Gulf of Guinea. It is known for Asante cultural heritage, woven kente cloth, and coastal forts that bear witness to the Atlantic slave trade.

photo.alt: Panorama over Town from Fort Victoria − Cape Coast − Central region

GI.description: Gibraltar sits at the southern tip of the Iberian Peninsula. Its limestone Rock contains extensive caves and tunnels and is home to a population of Barbary macaques.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner for Gibraltar. Cropped from this PD-licensed picture: http://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Gibraltar_Barbary_Macaques.jpg

GL.description: Greenland lies between the Arctic and North Atlantic oceans. It is known for its vast ice sheet, iceberg-filled fjords, and Inuit cultural traditions along its inhabited coasts.

photo.credit:
Original: Kim Hansen
derivative work: Jjtkk
photo.alt: The settlement Aappilattoq east of Upernavik in Greenland. Two handheld photographs taken with a Canon IXUS DIGITAL 800 IS stitched in Hugin ver. 0.7 beta 5. Cropped in GIMP and noise reduced with Noiseware.

GM.description: The Gambia follows the Gambia River inland from West Africa’s Atlantic coast. It is known for mangrove habitats, birdlife, and Mandinka kora music and storytelling traditions.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner: Fishing boat, Gunjur Gambia

GN.description: Guinea lies in West Africa, with Atlantic coastline and the highlands of Fouta Djallon. It is known for waterfall landscapes and influential traditions of percussion and dance.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner: Women fishing on River Niger in Guinea, Africa

GP.description: Guadeloupe is a Caribbean archipelago whose main islands resemble a butterfly. Rainforest and the volcano La Soufrière contrast with coral limestone landscapes and Creole cultural traditions.

photo.alt: Camera: Fuji G617 Film: Kodak E100 VS  The protohistoric site of Qubur Juhhal at Al Ayn lies near a palm grove in the interior of the Sultanate of Oman. Together with the neighbouring sites, it forms the most complete collection of settlements and necropolises from the 3rd millennium B.C. in the world. PR.description: Puerto Rico lies in the northeastern Caribbean. It is known for Old San Juan’s fortified streets, El Yunque’s rainforest, and musical traditions such as bomba and plena.

photo.alt: San Juan. Fort San Cristobal. Puerto Rico

PS.description: The Palestinian territories include the West Bank and Gaza in the eastern Mediterranean region. Their cultural heritage includes Bethlehem’s historic churches, olive-growing traditions, and distinctive embroidered textiles called tatreez.

photo.alt: Panoramic view from Qubeibe.

PT.description: Portugal sits on Europe’s Atlantic coast, known for its decorative azulejo tiles, historic maritime cities, and the terraced vineyards of the Douro Valley.

photo.alt: Chapel Of Souls (Capela Das Almas) in Porto, Portugal - Wikivoyage banner

PW.description: Palau is a western Pacific island country known for the forested limestone formations of the Rock Islands, coral reef ecosystems, and traditional meeting houses decorated with local stories.

photo.credit:
Jellyfish_Lake_aerial_(March_2008).jpg: Lukas from Munich, Germany
derivative work: Inkey
photo.alt: Jellyfish Lake on Eil Malk Island, Palau. Looking west-northwest with some coral and rock islets in the background. The Seventy Island Preserve is just visible in the upper left on the horizon. At the bottom of the image, in the lake, the numerous bright dots are the jellyfish.

PY.description: Paraguay is a landlocked South American country shaped by the Paraguay and Paraná rivers. It is known for Guaraní language and culture, ñandutí lacework, and the grasslands of the Chaco.

photo.credit: Greg Schechter from San Francisco, USA
photo.alt: Jesuit Ruins of Trinidad and Jesus in Paraguay

QA.description: Qatar occupies a peninsula in the Persian Gulf. It is known for Doha’s Museum of Islamic Art, a maritime pearling heritage, and dunes meeting the tidal waters of Khor Al Adaid.

photo.alt:
Original Flickr description: A view along Doha's Corniche on a November afternoon.

Derived into banner format for use on Wikivoyage.

RE.description: Réunion is a volcanic island in the Indian Ocean. It is known for the active Piton de la Fournaise, steep mountain cirques, and Creole traditions blending multiple cultural influences.

photo.alt: Banner for La Réunion Island

RO.description: Romania lies in southeastern Europe around the Carpathian Mountains. It is known for Transylvania’s fortified churches, Maramureș’ wooden architecture, and the wetlands of the Danube Delta.

photo.credit:
Panorama_Fan_Festival.jpg: El bes
derivative work: Jjtkk
photo.alt: Panoramaphoto from the Fan Festival that is a protest event against the gold mining project in Roşia Montană, Romania. On the left you see part of the existing gold mine

RS.description: Serbia lies in the central Balkans, where the Danube and Sava meet at Belgrade. It is known for medieval monasteries, distinctive frescoes, and traditions of brass music.

photo.alt: Panoramic image of Danube pictured in Ritopek, suburb of Belgrade, Serbia.

RU.description: Russia spans eastern Europe and northern Asia. It is known for Saint Petersburg’s imperial architecture, Lake Baikal, and the vast forests and landscapes of Siberia.

photo.alt: landscapes Izborsk Valley

RW.description: Rwanda lies in East Africa’s Great Lakes region. It is known for mountain gorillas in the Virunga landscape, the montane rainforest of Nyungwe, and intricate basket-weaving traditions.

photo.credit: Andrew Moore from Johannesburg, South Africa
photo.alt: I was in Musanze, Rwanda, for work. The city is the gateway to visit the gorrillas, but I did not have the time nor resources to get out to them. However, the volcanoes are there for all to see!

SA.description: Saudi Arabia occupies much of the Arabian Peninsula. It is known for the rock-cut tombs of Hegra, Jeddah’s historic coral-stone buildings, and the desert landscapes of the Empty Quarter.

photo.credit: Omar Chatriwala of Al Jazeera English
photo.alt: Saudi Arabia page banner, for use on Wikivoyage

SB.description: The Solomon Islands form a Pacific archipelago east of Papua New Guinea. They are known for coral lagoons, traditional shell money, and maritime heritage around islands such as Malaita.

photo.alt: Kennedy Island (colloquially known as Plum Pudding Island though the correct local name is Kasolo Island) is an island in the Solomon Islands that was named after John F. Kennedy.

SC.description: Seychelles is an Indian Ocean archipelago off East Africa. It is known for granite-framed beaches, giant tortoises, and the distinctive coco de mer palms of the Vallée de Mai.

photo.credit: NOTE: This image is a panorama of Seychelles consisting of multiple frames that were merged or stitched in Panorama Studio. As a result, this image necessarily underwent some form of digital manipulation. These manipulations may include blending, blurring, cloning, and color and perspective adjustments. As a result of these adjustments, the image content may be slightly different from reality at the points where multiple images were combined. This manipulation is often required due to lens, perspective, and parallax distortions.
photo.alt: Seychelles, port at Hotel Wharf

SD.description: Sudan lies along the Nile in northeastern Africa. It is known for the pyramids of Meroë, the archaeological remains of ancient Kush, and desert landscapes dotted with Nubian settlements.

photo.credit:
Sudan_-_the_black_pharaohs.jpg: Retlaw Snellac
derivative work: JamesA
photo.alt: A view of the Meroe Pyramids in Sudan.

SE.description: Sweden stretches from Baltic archipelagos to Arctic Lapland. It is known for Stockholm’s island setting, forests and lakes, and a design tradition combining craftsmanship with practical simplicity.

photo.alt: Marmorbruket

SG.description: Singapore is an island city-state at the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula. It is known for hawker food culture, historic shophouses, and gardens woven into its dense urban landscape.

photo.alt: The Supertree Grove at Gardens by the Bay, Singapore. (ISO constant at 50 with HDR.)

SH.description: Saint Helena, Ascension, and Tristan da Cunha are remote South Atlantic islands. Saint Helena’s volcanic valleys, Ascension’s seabirds, and Tristan’s isolated settlement give the group contrasting identities.

photo.alt: Disambiguation page banner based on PD Swedish road sign image

SI.description: Slovenia lies between the Alps and the Adriatic. It is known for Lake Bled, the limestone caves of the Karst region, and the emerald waters of the Soča River.

photo.alt: Izlake panorama

SJ.description: Svalbard and Jan Mayen are Arctic island territories. Svalbard is known for glaciers and polar wildlife, while Jan Mayen is dominated by the volcanic peak of Beerenberg.

photo.alt: View across the Advent fjord from the Port of Longyearbyen on Spitsbergen on a cold morning in March 2015. The two mountains across the fjord are Adventfjellet, to the left, and Hjorthfjellet to the right.

SK.description: Slovakia is a Central European country known for the High Tatras, medieval castles such as Spiš, and traditional wooden churches in its Carpathian mountain villages.

photo.credit:
Spis_Castle_01.JPG: József Süveg
derivative work: Danapit
photo.alt: This media shows the protected monument with the number 810-830/1 CHMSK/810-830/1,CHMSK/810-830(other) in the Slovak Republic.

SL.description: Sierra Leone lies on West Africa’s Atlantic coast. It is known for the beaches of the Freetown Peninsula, the history of Bunce Island, and rainforest habitats in the Gola region.

photo.alt: Beautiful beach in west Africa just an hour's drive from Freetown.

SM.description: San Marino is a small country surrounded by Italy. Its medieval center rises on Mount Titano, where three hilltop towers overlook the surrounding countryside.

photo.alt: Guaita tower in San-Marino

SN.description: Senegal lies on West Africa’s Atlantic coast. It is known for mbalax music, Saint-Louis’ historic island district, and Gorée Island’s role in remembering the Atlantic slave trade.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner for Senegal. Cropped from this PD-licensed picture:http://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Senegal_624.jpg

SO.description: Somalia occupies much of the Horn of Africa, with long Indian Ocean and Gulf of Aden coastlines. It is known for poetry, nomadic pastoral traditions, and historic maritime trading towns.

photo.alt: A view of Lido beach from the sea in Mogadishu, Somalia on 15 November 2019.

SR.description: Suriname lies on South America’s northern coast. It is known for Paramaribo’s wooden architecture, extensive tropical rainforest, and cultural traditions reflecting indigenous, Maroon, Asian, and European heritage.

photo.alt: Suriname banner

SS.description: South Sudan lies in East-Central Africa along the White Nile. It is known for the vast Sudd wetlands, seasonal wildlife migrations, and the pastoral traditions of its diverse communities.

photo.credit:
Huts_in_Yei_township,_South_Sudan.jpg: SuSanA Secretariat
derivative work: JamesA
photo.alt: Straw huts in Yei township, South Sudan.

ST.description: São Tomé and Príncipe is an island country in the Gulf of Guinea. It is known for volcanic rainforest landscapes, former cocoa estates, and the dramatic rock tower of Pico Cão Grande.

photo.alt: Egg of Prinia molleri. Collection of Jacques Perrin de Brichambaut.

SV.description: El Salvador lies on Central America’s Pacific coast. It is known for volcanic lakes, the archaeological site of Joya de Cerén, and pupusas, thick stuffed corn tortillas central to local cuisine.

photo.alt: ​清晨时分的圣萨尔瓦多天际线

SX.description: Sint Maarten occupies the southern part of a Caribbean island shared with Saint Martin. It is known for Philipsburg’s waterfront, Simpson Bay’s lagoon, and a lively blend of island cultures.

photo.alt: Panorama of Orient Beach in Saint Martin; Saint Martin banner

SY.description: Syria lies in the eastern Mediterranean region. Its heritage includes the ancient city of Damascus, Aleppo’s citadel, and Palmyra’s desert ruins, reflecting centuries of trade and cultural exchange.

photo.alt: Banner with Palmyra, Syria

SZ.description: Eswatini is a southern African country between South Africa and Mozambique. It is known for the Umhlanga reed dance, the landscapes of the Ezulwini Valley, and skilled weaving traditions.

photo.credit:
Swaziland_-_Traditional_homes.jpg: Caitlin from Hertfordshire, UK
derivative work: Jjtkk
photo.alt: Traditional homes in Eswatini and still widely used outside of the towns

TC.description: The Turks and Caicos Islands lie southeast of the Bahamas in the Atlantic. They are known for long coral sand beaches, shallow turquoise banks, and salt-trading heritage on smaller islands.

photo.credit:
Chalk_Sound.jpg: Tim Sackton
derivative work: Jjtkk
photo.alt: Chalk Sound has some of the most uniform turquoise water I have ever seen. Taken February, 2011 in Chalk Sound, Providenciales, Turks and Caicos Islands ¹⁄₄₀₀ sec at f/11, ISO200, no flash.

TD.description: Chad stretches from the Sahara into Central African savannas. It is known for the sandstone formations of the Ennedi Plateau, the Lakes of Ounianga, and wildlife in the Zakouma region.

photo.credit:
File:Ancienne ville d'Ouara, Ouaddaï, Chad.jpg: Robertgrafl
derivative work: Jjtkk
photo.alt: ancienent city of ouara, chad

TF.description: The French Southern Territories include remote Indian Ocean islands such as Kerguelen and Crozet. Their volcanic landscapes support scientific research and large breeding colonies of seabirds and marine mammals.

photo.credit:
Port_aux_Français.JPG: Daniel Delille
derivative work: Inkey
photo.alt: Port-aux-Français - French Station located in the Kerguelen Archipelago. Back : Golfe du Morbihan.

TG.description: Togo is a narrow West African country extending inland from the Gulf of Guinea. It is known for the earthen tower houses of Koutammakou and Lomé’s markets and textile traditions.

photo.credit:
Fishing_net,_Togo.jpg: Ferdinand Reus from Arnhem, Holland
derivative work: Jjtkk
photo.alt: Fishermen in Togo, December 2007.

TH.description: Thailand lies in Southeast Asia, with forested northern mountains and tropical southern coastlines. It is known for Buddhist temple architecture, regional street food, and the historic cities of Ayutthaya and Sukhothai.

photo.alt: Phai Ling, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya District, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, Thailand

TJ.description: Tajikistan is a mountainous Central Asian country dominated by the Pamir and Fann ranges. It is known for high-altitude lakes, Persian-speaking cultural heritage, and settlements along former Silk Road routes.

photo.alt: The Pamir Highway in Tajikistan near the Karakul lake.

TK.description: Tokelau consists of three remote coral atolls in the South Pacific. Lagoon fishing, woven crafts, and strong community traditions shape life across Atafu, Nukunonu, and Fakaofo.

photo.alt: A barge leaves the dock at Nukunonu in Tokelau to collect passengers and cargo from the MV Tokelau drifting in deeper waters in the distance; Tokelau baner

TL.description: Timor-Leste occupies eastern Timor and nearby islands in Southeast Asia. It is known for Mount Ramelau, the coral habitats around Atauro, and handwoven textiles called tais.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner

TM.description: Turkmenistan lies in Central Asia between the Caspian Sea and the Karakum Desert. It is known for ancient Merv, intricate carpet-weaving traditions, and the archaeological remains of Nisa.

photo.alt: Carpets of Turkmenistan

TN.description: Tunisia lies on North Africa’s Mediterranean coast. It is known for ancient Carthage, Kairouan’s religious architecture, and southern landscapes of desert oases and fortified granaries.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner for Tunisia. Cropped from this PD-licensed picture: http://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Tunis_Carthage_Villa_romaine_5.jpg

TO.description: Tonga is a Polynesian island country in the South Pacific. It is known for the Haʻamonga ʻa Maui stone monument, tapa cloth traditions, and humpback whales in its surrounding waters.

photo.alt: Royal Sunset Island Resort at 'Atata Island, 30 min boat ride from Tongatapu.

TR.description: Turkey spans southeastern Europe and western Asia. It is known for Istanbul’s layered architectural heritage, Cappadocia’s rock formations, and regional traditions of ceramics, carpets, and cuisine.

photo.credit:
1. Sevtap On
2. Bjørn Christian Tørrissen
3. Derrick Brutel

4. Kerem Barut
photo.alt: Kekova (Turkey) banner

TT.description: Trinidad and Tobago lies near Venezuela in the southern Caribbean. It is known for Carnival, the invention of steelpan, and Tobago’s forested hills and coral reefs.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner for Trinidad and Tobago. Cropped from this PD-licensed picture:File:Pigeon_Point_Tobago_fr_Water.jpg

TV.description: Tuvalu is a Pacific island country made up of low coral islands and atolls. It is known for Funafuti’s lagoon and fatele performances combining song, rhythmic clapping, and dance.

photo.alt: Tuvalu

TW.description: Taiwan is a mountainous island in the western Pacific. It is known for lively night markets, tea-growing hills, and cultural traditions shaped by indigenous communities and successive waves of migration.

photo.alt: Formosa Boulevard Station banner

TZ.description: Tanzania lies in East Africa along the Indian Ocean. It is known for Serengeti wildlife migrations, Mount Kilimanjaro, and the Swahili trading heritage of Zanzibar’s Stone Town.

photo.credit:
Inside_Ngorongoro_crater.jpg: Muhammad Mahdi Karim
derivative work: JamesA
photo.alt: Inside the Ngorongoro crater, tourists looking at animals. The background features the rim of the crater.

UA.description: Ukraine lies in Eastern Europe between the Carpathians and the Black Sea. It is known for Kyiv’s historic churches, Lviv’s architectural heritage, and traditional embroidered textiles called vyshyvanka.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner of Chernivtsi (Ukraine)

UG.description: Uganda lies in East Africa’s Great Lakes region. It is known for Bwindi’s mountain gorillas, the Rwenzori Mountains, and the Nile’s powerful passage through Murchison Falls.

photo.alt: Uganda

UM.description: The United States Minor Outlying Islands are scattered across the Pacific and Caribbean. They include remote coral islands and atolls such as Midway, known for extensive seabird colonies.

photo.credit: U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class Mark Logico
photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner: PEARL HARBOR (June 2, 2010) More than a million Laysan Albatrosses, also known as "gooney birds" overwhelmingly occupy the entire Midway atoll. (U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class Mark Logico/Released)

US.description: The United States spans much of North America and extends into the Pacific. It is known for national park landscapes, diverse regional cultures, and musical traditions including jazz and blues.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner: Statue of Liberty, NY, in sunlight

UY.description: Uruguay lies on South America’s Atlantic coast beside the Río de la Plata. It is known for Montevideo’s waterfront, Colonia del Sacramento’s historic streets, and candombe drumming traditions.

photo.alt: Panorámica de la playa de Pocitos en Montevideo (Uruguay)

UZ.description: Uzbekistan lies in Central Asia along historic Silk Road routes. It is known for Samarkand’s tiled monuments, Bukhara’s trading domes, and the walled old city of Khiva.

photo.alt: Samarkand

VA.description: Vatican City is a small city-state enclosed by Rome. It is known for St. Peter’s Basilica, the Vatican Museums, and the Renaissance frescoes of the Sistine Chapel.

photo.alt: Cropped version of: http://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Creaci%C3%B3n_de_Ad%C3%A1n.jpg

VC.description: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines stretches across volcanic and coral islands in the Caribbean. It is known for La Soufrière’s mountain landscape and the reef-fringed waters of the Tobago Cays.

photo.alt: Palm Island, Saint Vincent and The Grenadines

VE.description: Venezuela lies on South America’s northern coast. It is known for Angel Falls, the table mountains of Canaima, and the plains of the Orinoco Basin.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner for Venezuela. Cropped from this PD-licensed picture:File:Canaima_panoramic.jpg

VG.description: The British Virgin Islands lie in the northeastern Caribbean. They are known for sheltered sailing waters, the granite boulders of Virgin Gorda’s Baths, and coral-fringed island coastlines.

photo.alt: sailboats at Tortola, Wikivoyage banner for the British Virgin Islands

VI.description: The U.S. Virgin Islands lie in the northeastern Caribbean. They are known for St. John’s protected coastal landscapes, Charlotte Amalie’s historic harbor, and Crucian cultural traditions on St. Croix.

photo.alt: Turtle Bay Beach at Caneel Bay Resort, St John, US Virgin Islands

VN.description: Vietnam stretches along Southeast Asia’s eastern coast. It is known for Hạ Long Bay’s limestone islands, Hội An’s historic trading streets, and regional food traditions shaped by rice and fresh herbs.

photo.alt: File:HaLongBayBIG.jpg resized and cropped for use as a Wikivoyage banner

VU.description: Vanuatu is a volcanic South Pacific archipelago known for Tanna’s Mount Yasur, diverse island languages, and sand drawing traditions. Customary community life is an important part of its cultural identity.

photo.alt: Eratap beach, Efate, Vanuatu,

WF.description: Wallis and Futuna is a South Pacific island group. It is known for the fortified archaeological site of Talietumu, volcanic lake landscapes, and Polynesian traditions of ceremony and craftsmanship.

photo.alt: Alofitaï beach, Alofi Island; Wallis and Futuna banner

WS.description: Samoa is a Polynesian country in the South Pacific. It is known for open-sided fale houses, intricate tatau tattooing, and the village and family traditions of fa’a Samoa.

photo.alt: Lalomanu Beach with Nu'utele island off the east coast of Upolu in Samoa.  Panorama made from 6 photos in potrait

YE.description: Yemen lies at the southwestern end of the Arabian Peninsula. It is known for Sana’a’s decorated tower houses, Shibam’s earthen architecture, and Socotra’s distinctive dragon’s blood trees.

photo.credit:
Shibam_Wadi_Hadhramaut_Yemen.jpg: Jialiang Gao www.peace-on-earth.org
derivative work: JamesA
photo.alt: The high-rise architectures at Shibam, Wadi Hadhramaut (or Hadhramout, Hadramawt) Yemen. For use on Wikivoyage.

YT.description: Mayotte lies in the Mozambique Channel between Madagascar and East Africa. It is known for a broad coral lagoon, volcanic hills, and cultural traditions connected with the Comorian archipelago.

photo.alt: Un maki de l'île de Mayotte.

ZA.description: South Africa lies at Africa’s southern tip. It is known for Table Mountain, the wildlife landscapes of Kruger, and cultural traditions spanning many languages, communities, and musical styles.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner: Cape Town, South Africa

ZM.description: Zambia lies in southern Africa along the Zambezi River. It is known for Victoria Falls, shared with Zimbabwe, and the floodplain and woodland wildlife habitats of the Luangwa Valley.

photo.alt: Wikivoyage banner for Zambia. Cropped from this PD-licensed picture:http://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:08-18-06_-_Kundalila_Falls_VIII.jpg

ZW.description: Zimbabwe is a landlocked southern African country known for the stone ruins of Great Zimbabwe, the granite landscapes of Matobo, and Victoria Falls on the Zambezi River.

photo.credit:
Victoria_Falls_from_Zimbabwe.jpg: Chris Eason from London
derivative work: Jjtkk
photo.alt: Victoria Falls from the Zimbabwean side
